RagShortTexts: Markets need checks of scales, weights and containers with locally accepted standards.
Marks aid recognition but do not replace weighing or establish quality.

Variants.Content:
For grain, wax or metal, both parties must know whether a weighing means net goods, goods with a sack or an agreed package. Tampered beams, cords and weights accumulate small differences into substantial loss. Traders compare familiar weights or seek market witnesses; a shared method makes agreement possible.

Owners’ marks and recognised stamps identify equipment without proving every use correct. Foreigners may not understand local units, and interpreters or intermediaries can favour a party. Opening, reweighing and agreeing tare at the market is easier than pursuing a claim far away. Dishonest sellers exploit haste and unfamiliar onlookers.
Market leaders need ways to reweigh and hear claims. Collecting dues while ignoring false weights discourages honest suppliers.
Ration collection needs checks of containers, adulteration and short weight. A shared handover weighing helps prevent every later shortage being charged to the escort.
Small sellers also lose from short weighing and value trusted neighbours as witnesses. Buyers inspect the goods and packing as well as marks on weights.
